newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin's address slows down Russian shares fall.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin's address slows down Russian shares fall.

text.p: Leading Russian shares slipped on Thursday on small-scale selling by local brokers, but comments by President Boris Yeltsin steadied the market, traders said.
The Russian Trading System index of 24 shares fell by 0.27 percent to 163.45 on $11.99 million in volume.
"I can see a slow, but sure decline," said Alexander Alexeyev. a trader from Russian Brokerage House.
He said Thursday's address by President Boris Yeltsin was evaluated optimistically by the market.
"The market has stabilised after this," he said. "Traders expected the prices to fall more."

Yeltsin said in a radio broadcast from hospital, where he is preparing for heart surgery, that he was still in control. He also expressed support for his security chief Alexander Lebed, who has been criticised by the opposition and some ministers for the settlement he negotiated in Chechnya.
Boris Shvedsky,a trader from IK Aton, said brokers tended to buy shares of those companies, which had issued or planned to issue American Depositary Receipts.
Chernogorneft rose to $7.30 from $6.85 on September 30, when the previous deal was registered and Mosenergo fell to $0.853 from $0.866 at Wednesday's close.
Alexeyev said the news that LUKoil and Agip signed a letter of intent to explore an oilfield in Siberia with an investment exceeding $220 million had no impact on LUKoil prices.
LUKoil was traded at $9.07 after $9.08 at Wednesday's close.
Alexeyev said prices would fall slowly with separate small rises until the news about Yeltsin's heart operation appeared.
"I do not expect any serious changes tomorrow," Shvedsky said. "The market is more or less stable."
Lenenergo rose to $0.389 from $0.390 at Wednesday's close, Norilsk Nickel rose to $6.23 from $6.18, UES fell to $0.0716 from $0.0721 and Irkutskenergo fell to $0.0920 from $0.0968.
